items.text: SUBJECTVOCABULARY

items.label: text
items.text: It is again easyto see that this equation involves a deprotonation-two of the waterligands transfer a hydrogen ion to the ammonia molecules.

items.label: text
items.text: solution.The equationfor thisreaction is:

items.label: formula
items.text: [Cu(H₂O)₄(OH)₂] + 4NH₃ → [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺ + 2H₂O + 2OH⁻

items.label: text
items.text: This is a ligand exchange reaction -four ammonia molecules replace two water molecules and two hydroxide ions.The solutions at the start and end of the reaction and the intermediate precipitate are shown in fig B.

items.label: section_header
items.text: FORMATIONOF[CuCI4]2-:CHANGEINCOORDINATIONNUMBER

items.label: text
items.text: These reactions always involve a change of ligand as well as a change in coordination number. A good example is the reaction between copper(Il) sulfate solution and concentrated hydrochloric acid. When the acid is added slowly and continuously,the colour gradually changesfrom blue togreen andfinallytoyellow.This is theequationforthereaction:

items.label: formula
items.text: [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ + 4Cl⁻ ⇌ [CuCl₄]²⁻ + 6H₂O

items.label: text
items.text: The state symbols, all (aq), have been left out for clarity.

items.label: text
items.text: You cansee that all sixwaterligands have been replaced byfour chloride ions.Thisreaction is also complexhaschangedfrom2+to2-,therehasbeennochangeinoxidationnumber

items.label: text
items.text: The arrowshowsthatthereactionisreversible,whichhelpstoexplainthecolourchangeobserved. The hexaaquacopper(Il) ion isblue and thetetrachlorocuprate(Il) ion is yellow,so thegreencolour is dueto a mixtureoftheblue andyellowcomplexions.Thesolutionsat thestart and endofthe reaction and the intermediate mixture are shown in fig C.

items.text: LEARNINGTIP

items.label: text
items.text: Youshouldrememberthecoloursofthespeciesinthesereactions,butyoudonotneedtounderstand whythespecieshavetheactualcolours.

items.label: section_header
items.text: AMPHOTERICHYDROXIDES

items.label: text
items.text: We have already seen that hydrated transitionmetal ions can be deprotonated by adding abase such as aqueous sodium hydroxide toform a precipitate of the metal hydroxide.For example, chromium(Il) hydroxide is precipitated from an aqueous solution containing Cr3+ ions:

items.label: formula
items.text:
[Cr(H₂O)₆]³⁺(aq) + 3OH⁻(aq) → [Cr(H₂O)₃(OH)₃](s) + 3H₂O(l)
green solution                green precipitate

items.label: text
items.text: When an excess of sodium hydroxide is added to this precipitate,further deprotonation can take place:

items.label: formula
items.text:
[Cr(H₂O)₃(OH)₃](s) + 3OH⁻(aq) → [Cr(OH)₆]³⁻(aq) + 3H₂O(l)
green solution

items.label: text
items.text: In this reaction, chromium(Ill) hydroxide is acting as an acid, since it is reacting with a base.

items.label: text
items.text: Chromium(IIl) hydroxide is also a base,because it can react with acids:

items.label: formula
items.text: [Cr(H₂O)₃(OH)₃](s) + 3H⁺(aq) → [Cr(H₂O)₆]³⁺(aq)

This is an example of amphoteric behaviour.
